I'm a 31-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with a high school education and some agricultural extension training. I manage 20 mu of land — not the biggest farm around, but enough that I need to think carefully about input costs and machinery use. My wife and parents help with labor, but I make the management decisions.

It's early October, so I'm starting with winter wheat planting. This year I'm keeping 15 mu in the wheat-maize double-crop system and putting 5 mu into cotton. Wheat-maize is my backbone — it gives me two harvests and spreads risk. If a drought hits one crop, the other might still do okay. Cotton is more work and more pesticide, but the profit per mu can be better, so I keep a small plot to diversify.

For the 15 mu of wheat, I'm buying improved seed. I stopped saving my own seed three years ago because the yield loss wasn't worth the small savings. I'll rotary till the fields and apply compound fertilizer as base — I'm targeting about 20 kg nitrogen per mu total, split between the basal dressing and a urea topdress at jointing in March. I'm also putting down about 12 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium per mu. The soil here is decent, but I don't want to cut corners and lose yield. I'll irrigate four times: winter irrigation in early December, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Four pesticide applications — pre-emergence herbicide, then two insecticide sprays for aphids and one fungicide if I see rust developing. I'm expecting about 525 kg per mu if the spring weather holds.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed — Nongda or Denghai varieties — directly into the wheat stubble with a no-till planter. There's no time to till between wheat harvest in early June and maize planting; the window is three days at most. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting, about 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations should be enough: one at the V8 stage and one at grain filling. Four pesticide sprays total — herbicide at pre-emergence, then insecticides for corn borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

The 5 mu of cotton I'll rotary till in April. Cotton needs more balanced nutrition, so I'm applying about 10 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. But the real cost is pesticide — I'll need 15 applications minimum for bollworm, aphids, and mites across the growing season. Two irrigations at flowering and boll development. If I get 300 kg per mu of seed cotton, that's a decent year.

I'm being careful with fertilizer — urea prices are still high, and I know from the extension materials that pushing nitrogen beyond 20-22 kg per mu on wheat gives diminishing returns. My neighbor applied 30 kg last year and only got 30 kg more yield, which wasn't worth the extra cost. But I also won't under-apply; I've seen what happens when you try to save 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer and lose 100 kg of yield. This plan keeps my family fed and gives me a cash cushion.
